title: Test tool-call arguments under both split and coalesced streaming delivery
applies_when: A streaming tool-call parser maintains name/argument/call-index state across increments, especially when a regex searches a buffer that can contain multiple calls.
lesson: Use the same valid generation with separate headers/arguments, whole-call delivery, several calls in one increment, and a complete first call plus partial next arguments. Compare reconstructed names, call indices and JSON values, including repeated function names and empty arguments. A greedy name match can span the next separator; returning after one state transition can lose arguments or attribute a later call to the wrong tool. Bound each call, process already-buffered arguments in the name-emitting increment, drain completed calls, and retain state until its explicit end marker. Exercise the real consumer's final flush: stored empty arguments can turn data loss into a plausible-looking empty object.
avoid_when: Respect the model's delimiter/token and caller contract: arbitrary character splitting of a single vocabulary marker is not automatically a production path. Do not demand byte-identical JSON if the API promises only equivalent JSON values. Component imports or unchanged extracted caller methods do not establish full installed-package/server/model correctness, unknown-tool behavior, arbitrary malformed-input recovery, performance, or upstream approval. A closed prior fix still deserves attribution; check active PR scope before opening another.

evidence.note: Independent Linux CPU comparison of complete DeepSeek V3 detector modules: main 234ccba and author heads 4581069/72cbf05 all lose the first of two coalesced calls. Both proposed fixes pass single-call and separately drained two-call controls but duplicate the last call under diagnostic empty increments; inherited finish() emits nothing. The known issue was already reported in #31915. Reproduction contributed to the original author, not a competing PR, new discovery or server/official-CI claim. Package initializers alone were bypassed; real Tool/base/JSON helpers were used.

Other-author Harmony repair at bb00fda98c3de8878ab80eed9198a361827fc64e: independent full stdlib parser audit preserved tool content/raw text for 341 split/coalesced delivery plans across both recipient header positions; main 35f3c96 failed 177 plans. Ordinary reasoning remains incremental. Component-only evidence, not our PR, official CI or a server/model qualification; character splits are defensive rather than a proven serving path. Live issue timeline revealed this PR when cached search did not.
Closed, unmerged prior report identifies first-increment argument loss in DeepSeek V3.1. It is prior work, not proof that current main contains the proposed repair.

Submitted CPU component reproduction and nine registered regressions cover coalesced DeepSeek V3.1 calls, partial arguments, repeated names, and final-flush behavior. Local component validation passes; full installed-package/server CI and maintainer approval are explicitly not claimed.

A separate open change tests split/coalesced parity for other detectors and distinguishes realistic token-boundary failures from character-level defensive hardening. This is supporting test design/prior work, not validation of the DeepSeek V3.1 repair.
